title: The Java Logging Habit That Costs You Nothing
description:
Most Java devs write log statements without thinking about the cost -- but SLF4J's `{}` placeholder syntax isn't just cleaner, it's how Logback skips building your log message entirely when that level is disabled. In this Short, see the real OrderService logging code from Level 4 of the Java Mastery Path and learn why concatenating strings in your logs quietly taxes every request in production.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/08-observability/

#Shorts

beats.narration: If you're still building log messages with string concatenation, you're doing work Java doesn't need -- on every single request.
Here's real Spring Boot logging code: SLF4J placeholders, not plus signs, tracking an order from creation through a declined payment to an unexpected failure.
Those placeholders aren't just tidy -- SLF4J only assembles that string if the log level is actually enabled. At INFO in production, your DEBUG logs cost you nothing, not even string-building.

display.heading: Why it's free
display.subheading: {} placeholders avoid building the message string at all when the log level is disabled

beats.narration: That's the difference between logging that scales and logging that quietly taxes every request. Full lesson's linked below.
